reports.name: USDA Weekly Export Sales (delayed by Veterans Day)

outlook: USDA's November reports lifted row crops on Tuesday. USDA cut the US corn yield to 179.6 bu/acre from 181.2 (trade expected about 180.6), dropping production to 15.89 billion bushels and ending stocks to 1.758 billion, well under the 1.846 billion trade guess; December corn finished near $4.48, up about 9 cents. Soybean yield rose only to 53.3 bu/acre, short of the bigger increase traders expected, and ending stocks fell to 300 million bushels, sending January soybeans up about 38 cents to near $12.27. Wheat ending stocks were nearly unchanged at 743 million bushels; Chicago wheat gained about 3 cents and Minneapolis spring wheat was up about a nickel at midday, with peace talks on Russia/Ukraine also in focus, while ICE January canola jumped C$13 to about C$770.
